subject: Standby-tier SLA contingency request and multi-region failover details
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@quantagrid.com>

Cc: QuantaGrid Procurement <procurement@quantagrid.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: standby-tier SLA and failover RTO/RPO for enterprise contract

Hi Hannah / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Before we move to procurement/PO, our legal and infra teams have two items that are blocking sign-off:

1) Concrete RTO/RPO commitments for a full-region outage (i.e., if our primary region becomes unavailable). We need numbers we can put into the MSA amendment and include in our internal runbooks. Please state expected recovery time ranges and the conditions under which those apply.

2) We are considering a lower-cost "standby-tier" option for budget reasons — the idea is a warm-burst standby (no full dedicated reserved capacity). For commercial reasons we need an exception in the SLA that reflects the standby-tier behavior (longer RTO window and some increased latency during failover). Can you propose explicit SLA language and the expected impact (p50/p95 latencies, any DTO to availability)?

Also: procurement asked for the runbook you referenced and any previous DR exercise reports or proof points (date of last full-region failover test, mean time to cutover in drills). SOC2 / audit evidence would be helpful too.

Target timeline for us is finalizing the amendment this month. Can you vendor this back with an action plan and a cost delta for the standby-tier exception vs. a dedicated failover commitment?

Thanks,
Ethan Cole
Director, Infrastructure Operations
QuantaGrid

Hi Ethan — thanks for the clear ask and the procurement note. High level answers below; I’ll follow up with a proposed amendment and a mutual action plan (MAP) by EOD tomorrow. I’ve also attached a concise runbook and a SLO comparison CSV to help with internal reviews.

Redwood standard (hosted multi-region):
- Monthly uptime SLA: 99.95% (standard public API tier).
- Failover behavior: active-standby routing with automated health checks; traffic routed to alternate region when primary is marked unhealthy.
- Typical automatic routing time: 10–20 minutes for networking-level reroute + service-level stabilization; for stateless requests (generation) this is generally <30 minutes.
- RTO / RPO guidance: for standard hosted customers we target RTO <= 60 minutes for a full-region outage and aim for RPO near-zero for request-forwarding (we preserve request acknowledgements where possible, but cached KV state is best-effort).

Standby-tier (budget warm-burst) — proposed exception:
- Offer: Warm-burst standby (capacity kept at reduced reserved level, auto-scale on surge).
- Proposed SLA amendment language (draft): "Customer electing Standby Tier acknowledges a contingency RTO window up to 2 hours for full-region failover and an RPO of up to 15 minutes for in-memory prefix/KV caches. Redwood will exercise best-effort preservation of in-flight sessions but cannot guarantee zero-loss for ephemeral cache state under Standby Tier."
- Expected latency impact during failover: p95 request latency may increase by ~25–40% for up to 24 hours while caches re-warm and cross-region traffic spikes; we will provide routing split metrics during the MAP.
- Runbook & evidence: attaching our standby-runbook summary and SLO comparison. We can redact internal drill telemetry but can provide aggregated drill results (time-to-route, median cutover) under NDA.

Dedicated reserved failover (higher commitment):
- With reserved warm capacity in target region we can commit to RTO <= 30 minutes and RPO < 1 minute for critical state (subject to contract language).

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll scope a MAP with milestones: draft amendment → legal review → procurement PO → docuSign.
2) Marissa (infra ops) will propose exact failover health-check hooks and thresholds.
3) We’ll include quarterly DR exercises as a contract KPI for the standby-tier, with agreed reporting cadence.

If this aligns with you, I’ll circulate the draft amendment today and a cost delta for Standby vs Dedicated by tomorrow morning.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: standby-tier SLA contingency request and multi-region failover details

Hannah — looping infra/ops notes so legal can see operational constraints we’d want captured. Quick bullets for the amendment (operationally accurate):

- Trigger definition: full-region outage must be declared by our cross-region health monitor (both control-plane and dataplane failures). Trigger event should be observable by both parties (we can share monitor IDs in the MAP).
- Warm-burst mechanics: standby-tier keeps N% reserved (configurable) — when CPU/GPU or concurrency crosses threshold, autoscale to full serving capacity. Cold-starts for larger quantized models can add time; for QW4 variants expect ~20–40 minutes additional to warm-up.
- RTO/RPO suggested language (opinionated): "In an event declared by Redwood as a Regional Outage, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to restore service within the RTO window. For Standby Tier customers, RTO may be up to 2 hours; RPO for replicated metadata and persistent customer data will be subject to configured replication intervals (default 15 minutes). Redwood will document replication topology in the MAP."
- Latency profile: expect transient p95 delta of +25%–35% on peak traffic for first 24 hours after cutover; we can commit to a p95 cap if customer upgrades to reserved warm capacity.
- DR exercises: recommend quarterly tabletop + annual full cutover for Standby Tier. If QuantaGrid agrees to quarterly drills and a small operational surcharge (we should model), we can reduce RTO target to 90 minutes after two successful consecutive drills.

I attached a short draft of the runbook and an operational checklist. Happy to convert these bullets into contractual language once Hannah has budget delta.

-Marissa
Director, Infrastructure Reliability
marissa_cole@redwood.com

We are prepared to accept the Standby Tier exception under the conditions you and Marissa outlined, with two asks before procurement signs:
1) Provide the draft amendment with the exact trigger definition and the RTO/RPO wording you proposed (we need the precise clause to run through legal).
2) Send a cost delta and an estimate of the operational surcharge for quarterly drills and the standby warm capacity.

If you can push a DocuSign-ready amendment and the cost table today, we’ll try to wrap this in our next procurement cycle and aim for signature by 09/10.

Thanks — Ethan
